rationale: Astra makes the acceptance rule concrete: the same 200 response passes for the invoice owner and fails for another tenant, then both checks run again after repair. Its larger labels and explicit ready-for-human-review ending make it the clearest main chapter entry for a team adopting agents. Keep baseline for session continuity and fable for the distinction between a completion claim, a test result and a persistent record.
findings: Astra 00:02.55–00:06.60 shows why an apparently successful response can be a failure against the agreed contract; baseline 00:03–00:06.40 and fable 00:03.10–00:07.65 leave the tested behavior abstract. Astra therefore gives the strongest first explanation of what a harness checks.

Baseline 00:09–00:16.50 uniquely shows the session disappearing while workspace and progress survive, followed by record reading, initialization and a smoke check. This is useful complementary teaching, although the short INIT/SMOKE transfers and anonymous tasks require more interpretation than Astra’s two visible expectations.

Fable 00:10.85–00:15.85 separates DONE B from RUN B, FAIL and a still-false feature row; at 00:22.60–00:24.60 a new pass permits the record update. This gives a clearer completion-claim lesson than baseline, while Astra supplies the more concrete reason for a failed check.

Astra 00:11.40 now clears both prior results in the same frame as PATCH 2, before fresh checks at 00:15.75 and 00:18.15. Baseline 00:22.40 and fable 00:24.60 retain A’s historical pass while recording B; their transcripts now explicitly avoid claiming that A was retested after B changed.

At 350px, Astra’s 00:06.30 failure and 00:24.50 resolved state have the strongest label hierarchy. Baseline’s 00:12.80 recovery state and fable’s 00:14.30 failed test remain readable but use smaller record labels and moving chips; baseline’s missing opening title has been corrected.

Astra 00:21.75–00:25.50 holds READY for human review, without implying deployment or approval. Baseline 00:22.40–00:25 and fable about 00:24.60–00:27 hold saved results instead; all endings resolve, fade and reach matching near-black bookends. Astra’s longer hold helps inspection but makes it slightly less brisk.
contentVerdict: Keep as core. Reproducible setup, executable feedback, current evidence and inspectable handoffs are immediate needs for a team transitioning to agentic engineering. The guide now makes advancement observable with a runner-owned ready-for-review marker withheld on failure, while distinguishing this local control from repository permissions. Primary documents support the patterns, not guarantees: prompted self-verification is not enforced isolation, saved passes can become stale, two authorization checks are incomplete, and branch rules depend on bypass settings, status sources and whether required tests actually ran.
defectsFixed: Baseline: added Resume work / HARNESS ENGINEERING identification and a full-frame fade; rerendered and regenerated its poster while retaining the original lesson and cue timing.

Astra: removed the 0.8-second stale-evidence interval by atomically clearing check values and colours when PATCH 2 appears at 11.40s; moved the invalidation cue with it, rerendered, and selected a resolved READY frame for the poster.

Baseline transcript: corrected interruption/resumption windows and clarified the limited scope of startup smoke checks and retained A evidence. Fable transcript: clarified that A is not visibly retested after edits to B; its encoded media remains byte-identical.

Guide: added source retrieval dates and explicit skipped/neutral-check and expected-status-provider boundaries; strengthened the exercise to verify that a failed check withholds a runner-owned readiness marker.
Preserved original source/media snapshots and original model provenance; added comparative-editor attribution and correction metadata. Baseline original model remains unrecorded.
limitations: Audio was analysed, not heard: decoded peak levels, spectrograms and energy near scheduled cues were checked. This does not establish subjective mix quality or independent audibility of overlapping cues.
Legibility was inspected in decoded full-size and exact 350px frames; no physical-phone test, continuous real-time viewing, or learner study was performed. Scores are comparative editorial judgments.

The videos are scripted illustrations. No real invoice implementation, agent reliability, actual end-to-end test suite or repository protection configuration was tested. Human review and harness-owned record writes are local design choices, not claims that every cited source uses them.

Blind review excluded author source, reviews, scores and declared model provenance until before.md was saved; filenames supplied by the user were known. Original author review/verification artifacts remain historical and are superseded for current media verification by harness-engineering/verification.json.
